evidence: A runnable calculation of clear, cloudless, aerosol-free air over ground of albedo 0.1, without refraction and without empirical check. The design column's line-by-line optics from 360 nm to 5 um (the sky model's 0.025 cm-1 visible grid, the radiative-convective model's near infrared) are grouped into 1504 channels that keep the absorbed energy within 1% on slant columns (reduction_check). The 282 channels below 1250 nm with whole-column absorption below 3 take the spherical sky model's multiple scattering at its standard quality; the others take the direct beam through the same spherical shells with the diffuse and reflected light of a pseudo-spherical two-stream column, so their twilight holds no scattered light. The flat and pseudo-spherical columns are the radiative-convective model's delta two-stream on the same 100 layers; PlaSim's is a copy of its clear-sky arithmetic on the solved column at the design run's levels and settings.
reading_rule: Global means are W/m2 over the whole sphere from the sunlight inside 360 nm-5 um, 1166.7 W/m2 at the beam, scaling with the run's sunlight; PlaSim's shares are applied to the same sunlight. The sphere is the reference; sphere_shallow is its light on the flat column's own layers, without the shells' widening above each square metre of ground. sphere_minus_pseudo_spherical is what the curved geometry adds to columns of the same air and optics, by class of solar elevation at the ground point and by GCM layer (top first), the sum of cone_w_m2 (the widening) and curved_light_w_m2 (the twilight, the side light and the curved scattered light); pseudo_spherical_minus_plasim is how PlaSim's calibrated arithmetic divides the same sunlight differently; sphere_minus_plasim is the whole clear-sky difference. by_elevation gives the absorption per square metre of ground per unit of sunlight at the beam (the whole covered spectrum), from which the sphere integral is 2 * integral of x d(sin a).

gcm_term.reading_rule: What the curved light adds to a flat column of the same air (curved_light_w_m2): the sphere's light on the flat column's own layers, less the pseudo-spherical column's, per square metre of ground per unit of sunlight at the beam, by the solar elevation at the ground point, to the ground and to each GCM layer (top first). Nothing outside the elevations given. Added to the GCM's own shortwave it keeps PlaSim's calibrated column and supplies the twilight, the low Sun's side light and the curved scattered light. The cone (cone_w_m2), the more sunlight the widening shells above each square metre take, is left out: those shells emit their infrared from the same wider area, which a flat model's longwave leaves out too.

cm1_term.reading_rule: gcm_term on the 100 shells of the design column instead of the GCM's layers, for a model on heights: what the curved light adds to each shell of a flat column (bottom-up, between the heights given) per square metre of ground per unit of sunlight at the beam, by solar elevation; the ground as in gcm_term.

shells_w_m2.reading_rule: The sunlight each of the design column's 100 shells absorbs (bottom-up), global means per square metre of ground, between the heights and pressures given: the sphere, its light on the flat column's volumes (sphere_shallow, so sphere_shallow / pseudo_spherical is the curved light's ratio of heating per unit mass) and the pseudo-spherical column.

cm1_term_cone.reading_rule: The cone the twilight terms leave out, by shell (bottom-up) and solar elevation, as in cm1_term: the more sunlight the widening shells above each square metre of ground take.

gcm_term_cone.reading_rule: The cone the GCM term leaves out, by GCM layer (top first) and solar elevation, as in gcm_term.

longwave.reading_rule: The infrared leaving the top of the design column (clear sky, its temperatures), W/m2 per square metre of ground: through flat layers, and through the same layers as spherical shells, which take in more sunlight (the cone and the curved light) and lose more infrared by the same geometry: the shells' widening (cone) and the escape below the horizontal past the Moon's limb (curved). By GCM layer (top first) and by shell (bottom-up) each with its design temperature, so a model may scale them with its own; the ground's share apart.
